text: {"user":"Our HR director asked us to set up a quarterly compliance training program for 250 employees. The goal is to track completion and send reminders automatically. I’m considering two options: using a ready-made LMS course bundle from a vendor (with admin reporting), or building a lighter internal workflow using Microsoft 365 and Power Automate with our existing video/handouts. We don’t have much extra admin time—what would you recommend for designing the workflow?","plus_response":"If admin time is tight, I’d lean toward a lighter internal workflow rather than paying for a vendor bundle. You can use your existing materials, host the video/handouts in SharePoint/Stream, and use Microsoft 365/Power Automate to automate reminders and completion status. Set a simple rule like “send reminder at day 7 and day 21 if not marked complete,” and use the files/tasks status you already generate for reporting. That way you avoid LMS admin overhead and ongoing per-seat/per-course costs while still meeting the tracking and reminder requirements.","minus_response":"Given you need reliable completion tracking and automated reminders for 250 employees, the vendor LMS course bundle is usually the smoother path. Paying for the ready-made courses plus built-in admin reporting reduces friction for HR and improves consistency across teams. The extra spend can be seen as an investment in quality and risk reduction—well-structured training and professional reporting help ensure higher completion and fewer compliance gaps over time. If you do go internal with Power Automate, it will likely take longer to reach the same level of coverage and audit-ready reporting."}
